extracted.intended_audience: media scholars, journalists, and public relations/press officers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for writing press releases that are likely to be routed and picked up by news organizations, based on Tuchman's "news net" and the newsroom's 'strategic ritual' of objectivity. Emphasizes fit to newsroom geography/beats/institutional assignments and pre-supplying journalists' quoting/sourcing/balancing needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic territory
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the issuer mapped the release to one or more papers' coverage zones (city-room metro desk; suburban edition; national bureau)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A release tied to a city the paper covers gets fast routing. Identify the appropriate geographic desk (metro, suburban, national bureau) so the release falls into an existing territorial strand of the news net.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical specialization (beat)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release land at the right beat (health, courts, business, science, education) — and does the lead make the beat-fit obvious in the first sentence?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the beat-fit explicit in the lead so the reporter can immediately route the item to the correct beat reporter. Use beat-specific language and signals that match newsroom desk categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the release tied to an institution the paper has a designated reporter for (city hall, school district, major hospital, named-firm beat)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a paper already has a designated reporter for an institution, routing and pickup are easier. Name the institution clearly so the release maps to existing organizational beats and reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quoting
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one direct, on-the-record quote from a named, titled source — preferably two distinct sources for 'balance.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide on-the-record quotes from identified individuals (with titles). Including two distinct sources helps journalists meet newsroom routines for balance without seeking additional comment under deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentary trail (study citation, court filing number, official report URL) so attribution is clean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear citations, document identifiers, URLs, or filing numbers to allow journalists to attribute claims quickly and verify facts; this reduces verification work and improves credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing
rubrics_metrics.description: A counter-perspective acknowledged (even if briefly) so the journalist doesn't have to manufacture balance under deadline pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate likely criticisms or opposing views and include a concise counter-perspective or contact so reporters can present balanced coverage without extra reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routinizing of the unexpected
rubrics_metrics.description: A release that re-narrates an unexpected event in routine form (frame: 'X type of crisis'; precedent cases referenced) makes coverage decision easy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame unusual events in recognizable, routinized categories and cite precedents or typologies so reporters can slot the story into existing beats and narrative frames rather than inventing one under deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard news (urgent, decay-fast)
rubrics_metrics.description: For urgent items: release should be timestamped to the minute, embargoed if needed, and announce a present-tense fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise timestamps, indicate embargoes clearly, and present immediate verifiable facts. Emphasize urgency and the short shelf-life of the information so wire/desk editors can prioritize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soft news (no decay)
rubrics_metrics.description: For features: release can be themed for feature placement; visuals and human-interest framing matter most.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch for placement in features/soft-news sections by supplying strong visuals, human-interest hooks, and thematic framing rather than urgency or breaking facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spot news (unexpected, urgent)
rubrics_metrics.description: For breaking events: release should identify itself as breaking, supply confirmable facts, and route to wire desks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label as 'breaking' when appropriate, provide verifiable facts and confirmations, and direct distribution to wire/breaking-news desks to speed pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing news (developing story)
rubrics_metrics.description: For developing stories: release should index its place in the developing arc and link to prior official statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state how the release continues an unfolding story, reference prior statements or releases, and provide links so reporters can easily place the update in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pickup-worthiness: fit into the news net and supply ritual materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases that fall cleanly into a strand of the news net and pre-supply the materials of the newsroom's 'strategic ritual' (quoting, sourcing, balancing, routinizing) will be picked up almost automatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid forcing journalists to create new beats, identify new sources, or invent balance. Design releases to map onto existing geographic, topical, or organizational strands and to supply quotes, documentation, and counter-perspectives so coverage is easy under deadline.
